about.headline: Andy Ebert
story: Andy was born in Wall-City, West Berlin, in November, 1971.

His enthusiasm for music was evident early on. He hit every decorative, but real drum in his grandparents’ house and played Rockstar on a plastic toy guitar. Shortly after, he discovered a real microphone his parents owned and started recording his voice to tape cassette. Being bored playing the organ and a few other instruments that were not inspiring to him he told his parents that he wanted to play the guitar. For his 10th birthday he received a classical guitar and started taking lessons right away.
Buying his first rock- and hard rock albums around the same time made him fall in love with the sound of the electric guitar, which set the mark for spending his whole life in the music business.
Within months he started playing with fellow musicians with a borrowed electric guitar, collaborating in a band setting.

Inspired by a few friends’ dads who also played guitar and owned other musical gear, too, he gained a great interest in all musical instruments and audio gear. Roaming the great music stores of West Berlin with a drummer friend, he bought his first Stratocaster guitar and a small amp. Studying a book on home recording he fell in love with that aspect of music and bought a little 6 channel mixer and some microphones. That gear and a tape deck became the studio set-up to record his band’s first demo tape in his parents’ basement where they also rehearsed. It was live to tape home recording. Eventually his band needed a vocal PA for rehearsals and their shows. He sold the 6-channel mixer and bought a 12-channel one with built-in power amps and a pair of wedges, which also acted as PA for their concerts.

An internship at a music store and the fact that his parents wanted him to have a “real” education lead to an apprenticeship in retail for musical instruments when he was 15. Customers ranged from amateurs to pros.

During the years working in music stores he expanded his home recording set-up to a 16-channel board, 8-track tape machine and wired up an additional room in the basement to have 2 recording rooms and a control room. Eventually that equipment was replaced by a 24-channel console, 16-track, ½” tape machine, and expanded by an even larger selection of mics and outboard gear.

In 1995 he changed jobs again and started working in wholesale for Sonor drums and Zildjian cymbals. In his spare-time he started mixing FOH for a friend’s band. His first experience as a live sound engineer. His boss at Sonor also had a local sound and lighting company and Andy started gigging for them after work and on weekends and kept recording more bands in his studio.

January 30th, 1997 became his first day as a professional touring FOH engineer, using 2 AUX sends as monitor outputs for stage amplification. The Golden Gospel Singers (& band) played predominantly in churches across Germany and some neighboring countries. Church acoustics are impossible to manage with a loud band and very few speakers. It was steep learning by doing.

After that tour wrapped he started working as a backline tech, and eventually ended up as a Sound Engineer, and occasional PA- and stage tech working for a large Audio company, TSE, in Berlin. From corporate shows with podium mics to hotel conferences, to bigger rock shows, he worked it all. This led to him mixing monitors at some larger events. He did really well and was hired in that position more often.

Following were national and European tours as monitor engineer. In spring 1999 he embarked on his first arena tour mixing monitors for one of the biggest German pop acts, Modern Talking, which led to a contact with Rocksound, the Scorpions sound company. Their “World Wide Live” video originally inspired Andy to wanting to become a sound engineer when it first came out in 1985. Touring for Rocksound and working for other larger scale Audio vendors in Germany caught the attention of Audio Rent / Clair Europe. They started hiring him for some tours, as a monitor engineer, as well as a monitor tech, mostly with US bands. Often, he ended up filling-in, or replacing the tours’ monitor engineer.

In 2003 Puddle Of Mudd sponsored his first US work visa. His first time in LA, he fell in love with the weather, the people and the music scene there. Fortunately, he met great people in LA that furthered his career and personality.
Since then he has been growing his portfolio of clients and has predominantly worked as a monitor engineer. Andy now resides in Venice, FL.
about.philosophy: At some shows I was allowed to mix the monitor sound. That was another incisive occurrence in my life and I knew — that is what I want to carry on with! I already knew a little bit about the psychology of mixing monitors, but I couldn't imagine that there would be a Mr. Bohlen who would primarily be responsible for my knowledge growing as much and as quickly as it did.
about.travel: To be a monitor engineer for Rocksound at the world exhibition Expo 2000 I had to move to Hannover for five months. Directly afterwards I toured for four months through half of Europe with a Gospel show again. In summer 2001 I worked for different companies at a couple of big festivals in Germany as local monitor engineer where I had the honor to mix the sound for some of my (teenage year) heroes.
about.behindTheScenes: From then on it was a fast way up. As well as my work at TSE I was touring as a backliner for some German artists and at some shows I was allowed to mix the monitor sound. Since Audio Rent I've been working with the most respected FOH engineers, production managers and tour managers worldwide.
funFacts: First guitar on his 10th birthday — Rock 'N' Roll for life
First live sound job as FOH in 1995; Golden Gospel Singers tour in early 1997
First major professional PA load-in: early Robbie Williams solo show, spring 1998
Monitor engineer for Modern Talking, 1999; Audio Rent – Clair Brothers Europe from 2002

media.biography: Andy Ebert is a monitor and FOH engineer based in worldwide touring production. Since going on the road in 1997, he has mixed monitors for artists including Alanis Morissette, The Weeknd, Maroon 5, Guns N’ Roses, Mariah Carey, Stone Temple Pilots, Neil Young, Velvet Revolver, Carrie Underwood, Adam Lambert, R.E.M., Dream Theater, and many others. He was nominated for the 2017 Parnelli Award for Monitor Engineer of the Year.
